gap_title: Consent framework lacks mandatory notice content, data minimisation, and withdrawal mechanisms
anchor_excerpt: 3.3 The Compliance department owns the Consent Management Control, which governs how and when consent is collected from Data Principals prior to processing their personal data.
suggested_text:
3.3 The Compliance department owns the Consent Management Control, which governs how, when, and for what purposes consent is collected from Data Principals prior to processing their personal data.

3.4 Prior to or at the time of seeking consent, NimbusPay shall provide every Data Principal with a notice that includes: (a) the specific categories of personal data to be collected; (b) the specific purposes for which such data will be processed; (c) instructions on how the Data Principal may exercise their rights under applicable data protection law, including access, correction, and erasure; and (d) details of how a complaint may be made to the Data Protection Board of India. The Compliance department shall maintain and periodically review the standard notice template used across all consent touchpoints.

3.5 Consent shall be sought only for the specific categories of personal data necessary for the specified purposes stated in the notice, in line with the data minimisation principles set out in Section 3.1. The Product Engineering department shall ensure that consent capture flows do not bundle unrelated purposes into a single consent request.

3.6 NimbusPay shall provide Data Principals with a self-service mechanism through the NimbusPay support portal (and equivalent in-app controls) to withdraw consent at any time, and withdrawing consent shall be as easy as giving it. Upon withdrawal, the Compliance department shall ensure that processing based on that consent ceases within 7 business days, without affecting the lawfulness of processing carried out prior to withdrawal.
final_text:
3.3 The Compliance department owns the Consent Management Control, which governs how, when, and for what purposes consent is collected from Data Principals prior to processing their personal data.

3.4 Prior to or at the time of seeking consent, NimbusPay shall provide every Data Principal with a notice that includes: (a) the specific categories of personal data to be collected; (b) the specific purposes for which such data will be processed; (c) instructions on how the Data Principal may exercise their rights under applicable data protection law, including access, correction, and erasure; and (d) details of how a complaint may be made to the Data Protection Board of India. The Compliance department shall maintain and periodically review the standard notice template used across all consent touchpoints.

3.5 Consent shall be sought only for the specific categories of personal data necessary for the specified purposes stated in the notice, in line with the data minimisation principles set out in Section 3.1. The Product Engineering department shall ensure that consent capture flows do not bundle unrelated purposes into a single consent request.

3.6 NimbusPay shall provide Data Principals with a self-service mechanism through the NimbusPay support portal (and equivalent in-app controls) to withdraw consent at any time, and withdrawing consent shall be as easy as giving it. Upon withdrawal, the Compliance department shall ensure that processing based on that consent ceases within 7 business days, without affecting the lawfulness of processing carried out prior to withdrawal.
rationale: This extends the existing Consent Management Control with mandated notice content, purpose-limited consent capture consistent with data minimisation, and an easy self-service withdrawal mechanism, addressing all three elements of the gap.

gap_title: Breach notification does not cover intimation to each affected Data Principal
anchor_excerpt: 6.3 In the event of a confirmed data breach involving personal data, the Information Security department shall notify affected Data Principals and the Data Protection Board of India without undue delay, and in any case within 72 hours of confirming the breach.
suggested_text:
6.3 In the event of a confirmed data breach involving personal data, the Information Security department shall notify the Data Protection Board of India in the prescribed form and manner, and in any case within 72 hours of confirming the breach.

6.4 In addition to notification to the Data Protection Board of India, the Information Security department, with support from the Compliance and Customer Support departments, shall give intimation of the breach to each affected Data Principal whose personal data was compromised, in the prescribed form and manner, without undue delay following confirmation of the breach. Such intimation to affected Data Principals shall include: (a) a description of the nature of the breach; (b) the categories of personal data affected; (c) likely consequences of the breach; (d) measures taken or proposed to address the breach; and (e) contact details for further information. Intimation shall be delivered through appropriate channels, which may include email, SMS, in-app notifications, or postal mail where electronic delivery is not feasible, using pre-approved communication templates maintained by the Compliance department.
final_text:
6.3 In the event of a confirmed data breach involving personal data, the Information Security department shall notify the Data Protection Board of India in the prescribed form and manner, and in any case within 72 hours of confirming the breach.

6.4 In addition to notification to the Data Protection Board of India, the Information Security department, with support from the Compliance and Customer Support departments, shall give intimation of the breach to each affected Data Principal whose personal data was compromised, in the prescribed form and manner, without undue delay following confirmation of the breach. Such intimation to affected Data Principals shall include: (a) a description of the nature of the breach; (b) the categories of personal data affected; (c) likely consequences of the breach; (d) measures taken or proposed to address the breach; and (e) contact details for further information. Intimation shall be delivered through appropriate channels, which may include email, SMS, in-app notifications, or postal mail where electronic delivery is not feasible, using pre-approved communication templates maintained by the Compliance department.
rationale: This change separates Board notification from individual notification and adds an explicit obligation, content requirements, templates, and delivery mechanisms for intimating each affected Data Principal, closing the gap against Section 8(6) which requires intimation to both the Board and each affected Data Principal.

gap_title: No event-driven erasure upon consent withdrawal or purpose completion
anchor_excerpt: 4.3 The Data Engineering department owns the Data Retention Control, which is implemented through automated deletion jobs running on the customer data warehouse.
suggested_text:
4.3 The Data Engineering department owns the Data Retention Control, which is implemented through automated deletion jobs running on the customer data warehouse.

4.4 In addition to time-based deletion, the Data Retention Control shall include event-driven erasure triggers that initiate erasure of a Data Principal's personal data across all NimbusPay systems upon (a) withdrawal of consent by the Data Principal, as recorded in the Consent Management Control, or (b) completion of the processing purpose for which the personal data was collected, subject to any retention obligations under applicable law (e.g., KYC records retained per Section 4.1).

4.5 Upon an event-driven erasure trigger, Data Engineering shall propagate deletion instructions to all downstream systems and third-party processors holding the affected personal data, and shall confirm and document processor-side erasure within 30 days of the trigger.
final_text:
4.3 The Data Engineering department owns the Data Retention Control, which is implemented through automated deletion jobs running on the customer data warehouse.

4.4 In addition to time-based deletion, the Data Retention Control shall include event-driven erasure triggers that initiate erasure of a Data Principal's personal data across all NimbusPay systems upon (a) withdrawal of consent by the Data Principal, as recorded in the Consent Management Control, or (b) completion of the processing purpose for which the personal data was collected, subject to any retention obligations under applicable law (e.g., KYC records retained per Section 4.1).

4.5 Upon an event-driven erasure trigger, Data Engineering shall propagate deletion instructions to all downstream systems and third-party processors holding the affected personal data, and shall confirm and document processor-side erasure within 30 days of the trigger.
rationale: This adds event-driven erasure triggered by consent withdrawal and purpose completion with downstream propagation, addressing Section 8(7) requirements absent from the purely time-based retention mechanism.

gap_title: No verifiable parental consent or child data protections
anchor_excerpt: 3.3 The Compliance department owns the Consent Management Control, which governs how and when consent is collected from Data Principals prior to processing their personal data.
suggested_text: 3.4 The Consent Management Control shall include an age-assurance mechanism that verifies the age of every user at the point of consent collection. 3.5 Where a user is identified as a child (below the statutory age threshold under applicable Indian data protection law), the Consent Management Control shall require verifiable parental consent, obtained through documented verification of the parent's or lawful guardian's identity, before any processing of the child's personal data. 3.6 For users identified as children, NimbusPay shall disable all tracking, behavioural monitoring, targeted advertising, and analytics profiling of the child's personal data, and shall not undertake such processing likely to cause detrimental effect on the child's well-being.
final_text: 3.4 The Consent Management Control shall include an age-assurance mechanism that verifies the age of every user at the point of consent collection. 3.5 Where a user is identified as a child (below the statutory age threshold under applicable Indian data protection law), the Consent Management Control shall require verifiable parental consent, obtained through documented verification of the parent's or lawful guardian's identity, before any processing of the child's personal data. 3.6 For users identified as children, NimbusPay shall disable all tracking, behavioural monitoring, targeted advertising, and analytics profiling of the child's personal data, and shall not undertake such processing likely to cause detrimental effect on the child's well-being.
rationale: This adds an age-assurance step at consent collection, a verifiable parental consent workflow for children below the statutory age threshold, and controls disabling tracking and behavioural monitoring of children, directly addressing Section 9 requirements.

gap_title: No independent data auditor engagement or periodic DPIA/audit process
anchor_excerpt: 8.2 This policy does not currently designate a named Data Protection Officer responsible for overseeing NimbusPay's compliance with applicable data protection law.
suggested_text: 8.2 The Board of Directors shall appoint a Data Protection Officer (DPO) responsible for overseeing NimbusPay's compliance with applicable data protection law, and the DPO's name and contact details shall be registered with the Data Protection Board of India. 8.3 The Compliance department shall engage an independent data auditor at least annually to assess NimbusPay's compliance with this policy and applicable data protection law, and shall publish the auditor's findings to senior management along with a remediation plan. 8.4 The Compliance department shall conduct a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) before initiating any new processing activity that is likely to result in high risk to Data Principals, and thereafter on a recurring basis at least once every twelve months for all high-risk processing activities.
final_text: 8.2 The Board of Directors shall appoint a Data Protection Officer (DPO) responsible for overseeing NimbusPay's compliance with applicable data protection law, and the DPO's name and contact details shall be registered with the Data Protection Board of India. 8.3 The Compliance department shall engage an independent data auditor at least annually to assess NimbusPay's compliance with this policy and applicable data protection law, and shall publish the auditor's findings to senior management along with a remediation plan. 8.4 The Compliance department shall conduct a Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) before initiating any new processing activity that is likely to result in high risk to Data Principals, and thereafter on a recurring basis at least once every twelve months for all high-risk processing activities.
rationale: This replaces the acknowledgment of a missing DPO designation with concrete provisions establishing DPO appointment and registration, independent annual data audits, and a recurring DPIA schedule owned by Compliance, directly addressing the accountability gap.

anchor_excerpt: 7.3 NimbusPay does not currently restrict which countries customer data may be transferred to when using cloud infrastructure providers.
suggested_text: 7.3 NimbusPay restricts cross-border transfers of personal data to countries and territories notified by the Central Government as permitted destinations under applicable data protection law. Transfers of personal data to any country or territory not so notified are prohibited. 7.4 The Compliance department owns the Cross-Border Transfer Control, which requires that all vendor data processing agreements include clauses restricting the transfer and storage of personal data to notified countries and territories only, and that vendor onboarding checks verify compliance with this restriction before personal data is shared with any third party.
final_text: 7.3 NimbusPay restricts cross-border transfers of personal data to countries and territories notified by the Central Government as permitted destinations under applicable data protection law. Transfers of personal data to any country or territory not so notified are prohibited. 7.4 The Compliance department owns the Cross-Border Transfer Control, which requires that all vendor data processing agreements include clauses restricting the transfer and storage of personal data to notified countries and territories only, and that vendor onboarding checks verify compliance with this restriction before personal data is shared with any third party.
rationale: This replaces the explicit admission of no transfer restrictions with a prohibition on transfers to non-notified countries/territories and embeds transfer-restriction clauses into vendor DPAs and onboarding checks, directly addressing the gap.

gap_title: No general grievance-redressal mechanism with timelines and escalation
anchor_excerpt: 5.3 The Compliance department owns the Data Subject Request Handling Process, which coordinates the response across Data Engineering, Product Engineering, and Customer Support.
suggested_text:
5.4 NimbusPay maintains a general Grievance Redressal Mechanism for complaints by Data Principals concerning the processing of their personal data, including but not limited to complaints that are not access, correction, or erasure requests under Sections 5.1–5.3. Complaints may be submitted through the NimbusPay support portal (selecting "Privacy Grievance"), by email to grievance@nimbuspays.com, or in writing to the registered office address.

5.5 The Customer Support department shall acknowledge every privacy grievance within 2 business days of receipt and forward it to the Compliance department within 3 business days. The Compliance department shall investigate and provide a resolution or a substantive interim response to the Data Principal within 30 calendar days of receipt of the grievance.

5.6 If a grievance is not resolved within 30 calendar days, or if the Data Principal is dissatisfied with the resolution, the Compliance department shall escalate the matter to the Chief Compliance Officer, who shall review and issue a final decision within an additional 15 calendar days. The Compliance department shall maintain a register of all grievances received, actions taken, timelines met, and outcomes communicated, which shall be reviewed as part of the annual policy review under Section 8.1.

gap_title: DSR Handling Process missing additional statutory obligations
anchor_excerpt: 5.3 The Compliance department owns the Data Subject Request Handling Process, which coordinates the response across Data Engineering, Product Engineering, and Customer Support.
suggested_text:
5.3 The Compliance department owns the Data Subject Request Handling Process, which coordinates the response across Data Engineering, Product Engineering, and Customer Support.

5.4 Before acting on any data subject request under Section 12(2) of applicable data protection law, the Compliance department shall verify the identity of the requesting Data Principal using reasonable verification measures proportionate to the sensitivity of the personal data involved, and shall document such verification in the request record.

5.5 The Compliance department shall respond to verified data subject requests within 30 calendar days of receipt, and where a request cannot be fulfilled, shall provide the Data Principal with a written explanation of the reasons for refusal and information on available grievance redressal mechanisms.

5.6 The Compliance department shall maintain a documented register of all data subject requests received, actions taken, response timelines met, and any refusals issued, which shall be retained as evidence of compliance with all obligations under Section 12.

gap_title: Unresolved conflict between 8-year KYC retention and data minimisation principles
anchor_excerpt: 4.3 The Data Engineering department owns the Data Retention Control, which is implemented through automated deletion jobs running on the customer data warehouse.
suggested_text: 4.4 Legal Conflict-Resolution Mechanism for Retention Obligations: Where a sector-specific regulatory retention mandate (such as the 8-year KYC and transaction record retention requirement under RBI recordkeeping norms) conflicts with the data minimisation and storage limitation principles of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, the Compliance department shall document and maintain a Legal Conflict-Resolution Mechanism that records: (a) the specific statutory or regulatory basis for each retention period; (b) an assessment of how the mandated retention period is reconciled with storage limitation duties, including restricting processing of retained personal data to the original purpose of legal compliance; (c) confirmation that erasure requests from Data Principals are evaluated against such overriding retention obligations before deletion; and (d) periodic review of whether the mandated retention period remains legally required. The scope of the Data Retention Control shall be updated to reflect this mechanism, ensuring that automated deletion jobs exclude records subject to documented overriding retention mandates while deleting all other personal data in accordance with Sections 4.1 through 4.3.
final_text: 4.4 Legal Conflict-Resolution Mechanism for Retention Obligations: Where a sector-specific regulatory retention mandate (such as the 8-year KYC and transaction record retention requirement under RBI recordkeeping norms) conflicts with the data minimisation and storage limitation principles of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, the Compliance department shall document and maintain a Legal Conflict-Resolution Mechanism that records: (a) the specific statutory or regulatory basis for each retention period; (b) an assessment of how the mandated retention period is reconciled with storage limitation duties, including restricting processing of retained personal data to the original purpose of legal compliance; (c) confirmation that erasure requests from Data Principals are evaluated against such overriding retention obligations before deletion; and (d) periodic review of whether the mandated retention period remains legally required. The scope of the Data Retention Control shall be updated to reflect this mechanism, ensuring that automated deletion jobs exclude records subject to documented overriding retention mandates while deleting all other personal data in accordance with Sections 4.1 through 4.3.
rationale: This addition establishes a documented legal conflict-resolution mechanism within Section 4 that reconciles the 8-year RBI KYC retention mandate with DPDP Act data minimisation and storage limitation principles and scopes the Data Retention Control accordingly.
